## Verdict: REJECT (one checklist FAIL at Important: the export_memories JSON round trip, VC-70)
The PR is not ready to merge: one Important checklist item failed and still failed after a re-verification. The JSON that `export_memories` produces does not parse through `parse_json`, so it cannot round-trip through the bundle import path.
Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings
### 🟠 Important / Major
- VC-70: FAIL (important) — export_memories JSON emits sql_pairs via SqlPair.model_dump(exclude_none=True) and schema_docs without training_type, producing a shape parse_json accepts for re-import with groups preserved. [src/sqllens/memory/admin.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  admin.py:379-388 export_memories JSON emits {"sql_pairs": [p.model_dump(exclude_none=True)...], "schema_docs": [...exclude training_type]}. SqlPair (schema.py:71-78) has only question/sql/groups, so no training_type leaks there, and SchemaDoc without training_type is accepted (default). BUT parse_json (io.py:153) does MemoryBundle.model_validate(raw), and MemoryBundle.sql_pairs is SqlPairsBlock | None (schema.py:130) with extra=forbid and a `pairs` field (schema.py:96-102). The export emits sql_pairs as a bare list, which fails validation against SqlPairsBlock (an object). So parse_json rejects the exported JSON whenever it is fed back; the claim that it produces a shape parse_json accepts is false. The shape is only the add_memories argument shape (admin.py:18-20), unlike serialize_json (io.py:203-206), which dumps the bundle in the block shape. Requirement: docs/internal/agent/memory.md:176-178 (unchanged in base and head) says JSON is canonical and round-trips losslessly with sql_pairs an object {training_type, pairs}.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (6)
<details><summary>6 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/memory/store.py`: `MemoryStore.set_groups` given an empty sequence strips both group keys from the merged dict, but Chroma merges metadata on update, so the old `memory_groups`/`memory_tagged` stay and the call silently does nothing. This is latent, because no current caller passes an empty list. (raised by 1/4 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/memory/importer.py` (`_NewItem`) and `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` (`DedupEntry`): `kind` is carried separately from the payload, so a mismatched pair can be built. This is latent. (raised by 1/4 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/memory/admin.py` lines 897-901: `get_memory_stats` leaves out of `unretrievable_count` any record that is marked tagged but whose group list cannot be read (`record_groups` returns `[]`). No request can retrieve such a record, and `list_memories`/`get_memory` show it as `groups: []`. (raised by 1/4 agents)
- VC-3: FAIL (suggestion) — Re-importing the same file saves nothing the second time. [docs/external/managing-memory.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Doc line docs/external/managing-memory.md:126 says 'Re-importing the same file is therefore safe and saves nothing the second time.' The two hinted cases hold: (a) dedup_entries (store.py:199-227) skips only rows with unparseable args_json, non-string/empty sql, or non-string question, but import only writes via add_sql_pair/add_schema_doc from SqlPair/SchemaDoc, whose validators (schema.py:56-57,85-95,119) reject blank text, so import itself does not create skipped rows; (b) sql_key (importer.py:50-64) runs sqlglot.parse + .sql(dialect='mysql') on the same stored text, which is deterministic, and falls back to stripped text, so the key matches on re-import. Counterexample though: the same table (managing-memory.md:121) documents `--clear`, which wipes the collection. import_bundle(clear=True) calls _baseline -> store.clear() then dedup_entries() (importer.py:164-172,202), so existing is empty, _plan puts every item in new_items (importer.py:140-143), and the loop saves all of them (importer.py:211-238, report.saved += 1). So re-importing the same file with --clear saves everything the second time. Also, items whose first-time save failed (importer.py:228-237) are saved on re-import. The absolute wording is therefore false for --clear, though it is accurate for a plain re-import without --clear. Minor doc imprecision; final state is identical.

  </details>

</details>

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The claim concerns chromadb 1.5 where-filter semantics (missing key vs $ne/$nin/$not_contains; $in/$eq on list metadata). The item has no dependency_sources, and the head view contains no chromadb library source (Glob for chromadb filter files found none; inventory.json matches for 'chromadb/' are the repo's own paths at lines 324-325). - VC-62: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — sql_key relies on sqlglot.parse(sql, read='mysql') returning a list that may contain None entries, and on Expression.sql(dialect='mysql') regenerating with string literal and identifier case preserved, so 'SELECT a FROM t' and 'select a\n from t' share a key while WHERE region = 'EU' and 'eu' do not. [src/sqllens/memory/importer.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  importer.py:50-64 does what the claim describes on its side. It filters None entries from sqlglot.parse(sql, read='mysql'), and when exactly one statement remains it returns ('parsed', stmt.sql(dialect='mysql')). requirements.txt:104 pins sqlglot==30.31.0. The claim depends on installed sqlglot runtime behavior (the parse return type and MySQL generator literal/identifier casing), but the item supplies no dependency_sources and sqlglot source is not in the views. I did not read the sqlglot parser or generator, so the claim is unverified. Missing evidence: sqlglot 30.31.0 source (parser.py, generator.py, dialects/mysql.py) or a run of the two example pairs.

  </details>

- VC-68: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — set_groups assumes chromadb collection.get(ids=...) returns found ids and metadatas aligned by position, and that collection.update merges metadata so keys left out survive. [src/sqllens/memory/store.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  src/sqllens/memory/store.py:229-257: set_groups zips got['ids'] with got['metadatas'] (so it relies on those two being aligned, not on ordering vs the requested ids), builds merged metadata dropping GROUPS_KEY/TAGGED_KEY, then calls collection.update(ids, metadatas). The comment at 254 asserts Chroma merges metadata on update. This is a library claim, but the item supplies no dependency_sources and the views do not vendor chromadb, so per the rules it can only be checked from the views, which hold no chromadb source. Not verified: chromadb Collection.update metadata merge-vs-replace semantics and get(ids=) result alignment in chromadb 1.5 (e.g. CollectionCommon.py / the segment metadata update path). Installed copies exist outside the supplied scope but were not used.

  </details>

- VC-100: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — The `chromadb` lower bound in `pyproject.toml` admits only releases that support list-valued metadata and the `$contains` filter on it, and that evaluate the metadata filter the retrieval uses the way 1.5.9 does for a record missing the filtered key. [pyproject.toml]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  criteria.json is a valid list and carries criterion 21, matching this item. pyproject.toml:35 declares `chromadb>=1.5,<2`. src/sqllens/_memory_groups.py:20,63 builds the filter from TAGGED_KEY `memory_tagged` and a `$contains` clause on the groups key. The claim depends on chromadb's runtime behaviour: validate_metadata for list values, `$contains` support, and how the filter treats records missing the key across 1.5.0 to 1.5.9. No `dependency_sources` were supplied and no chromadb source is in the views. A Glob for chromadb validator.py under the repo found nothing. Release-by-release behaviour cannot be settled from the repository alone. Missing evidence: chromadb 1.5.x source (validators, metadata filter evaluation) for the releases the lower bound admits.

  </details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A rule-set file whose rule sets carry `memory_groups` loads with `format_version = 1`. A rule-set file with no `memory_groups` anywhere loads as before this change. A `memory_groups` that is empty, holds a duplicate, or holds a non-string is refused at load like any other invalid rule-set field.
- [ ] While a rule-set file is configured, a `query_database` request under rule set S gets, from both the `search_saved_correct_tool_uses` tool and the automatic system-prompt memory context, only records that are untagged or share at least one group with S's `memory_groups`. A tagged record whose groups S does not list is never returned to a request under S.
- [ ] While a rule-set file is configured, a memory search with an empty group list (the request's rule set lists no `memory_groups`, or no rule-set selection is available to the search) gets only untagged records from both memory paths.
- [ ] A memory search under rule set S returns an in-scope record that clears the similarity threshold even when more records than the search's result limit, all outside S's groups, score higher.
- [ ] A record stored before the upgrade, while it remains untagged, is retrieved after the upgrade by requests under every rule set, with no re-import or migration step.
- [ ] Without a rule-set file, memory retrieval returns tagged and untagged records alike, as before this change.
- [ ] `sqllens verify-memory` run with `--rule-set S` retrieves memory exactly as a `query_database` request under S does.
- [ ] `sqllens import-memory`, the `import_memory` tool and the `add_memories` tool accept an optional `groups` list (non-empty, distinct strings) on each SQL pair and schema doc. An empty or duplicate-holding `groups` is a validation error.
- [ ] An import through any of those three surfaces that names a group no loaded rule set's `memory_groups` lists leaves the store unchanged, with nothing written and, for `sqllens import-memory --clear`, nothing deleted. The CLI exits non-zero and the tools return `isError: true`, and the message names every unknown group. With no rule-set file configured, any import that names a group is refused this way.
- [ ] An imported item that duplicates an existing record or an earlier item of the same import creates no second record and sets the groups of every record it matches this way: a tagged item onto a tagged record gives the union of both; a tagged item onto an untagged record gives the item's groups; an untagged item leaves the record's groups as they were. A duplicate that changed the record's groups is counted as updated, and one that changed nothing as a skipped duplicate. The updated count is shown as `updated=<n>` in the `sqllens import-memory` summary line, in the `import_memory` tool's report, and as `updated_count` in the `add_memories` result. A dry run reports the same counts without writing.
- [ ] Duplicate detection compares `sql` texts with sqlglot under the MySQL dialect: two texts match when each parses into exactly one statement and both regenerate to the same SQL, with string literals and identifiers keeping their case, so `WHERE region = 'EU'` and `where region = 'eu'` do not match while `SELECT a FROM t` and `select a\n  from t` do. When sqlglot raises any exception on either `sql` text while parsing or regenerating (`ParseError`, `TokenError` and `RecursionError` included), or the text parses into no statement or more than one, the two match only when their texts are identical after trimming leading and trailing whitespace, so re-importing the same file still saves nothing new. `question` texts match after collapsing whitespace and ignoring case, and `content` texts match as before this change.
- [ ] For a store in which no two records duplicate each other under the match rule, exporting it to JSON with `sqllens export-memory` or the `export_memories` tool and importing the result into an empty store recreates every record the export wrote, with the same groups, untagged records staying untagged, when every group the export names is listed in a loaded rule set's `memory_groups`. An export naming a group no rule set lists is refused on import like any other unknown group.
- [ ] A CSV export of a store holding at least one tagged record returns `lossy: true` from `export_memories`, and `sqllens export-memory` prints a `Warning:`. Both state how many records' groups were dropped. A CSV import never changes an existing record's groups.
- [ ] `list_memories` and `get_memory` return each record's groups. While a rule-set file is configured, `get_memory_stats` returns the count of tagged records none of whose groups appears in any rule set's `memory_groups`; without a rule-set file that count is 0.
- [ ] `get_access_rules` returns each rule set's `memory_groups`.
- [ ] `sqllens verify-memory` exits non-zero before running any case when its golden file has an item carrying `groups`, and the message names that item.
- [ ] The change leaves these unchanged: with a rule-set file configured, the agent has neither `save_question_tool_args` nor `save_text_memory`; and the memory admin tools (`list_memories`, `get_memory`, `export_memories`, `get_memory_stats`, `delete_memory`, `clear_memories`, `add_memories`) and `import_memory` act on every record for any caller, without regard to rule sets.
- [ ] `docs/external/rule-sets.md` documents `memory_groups` in the file reference and replaces the "Memory is shared by every rule set" limit with the group rule, still stating that the memory admin tools are not limited by rule sets and that SQL Lens trusts `_meta`.
- [ ] `docs/external/managing-memory.md` documents the bundle `groups` field, the unknown-group refusal, how duplicates combine groups, and that CSV carries no groups. Its paragraph beginning "Duplicate entries are skipped automatically" states the new match rule (SQL compared by sqlglot with literal and identifier case kept, exact text when the SQL does not parse) and that a duplicate which changes a record's groups counts as updated.
- [ ] `docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md` and `docs/internal/agent/memory.md` describe group-filtered retrieval. No doc or code comment states that memory is shared by every rule set as a fact; today that claim appears at least in `docs/external/rule-sets.md` (the "Nothing is saved to memory" and "Memory is shared by every rule set" bullets), `docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md` and the rule-set write-gate comment in `src/sqllens/agent/factory.py`.
- [ ] The `chromadb` lower bound in `pyproject.toml` admits only releases that support list-valued metadata and the `$contains` filter on it, and that evaluate the metadata filter the retrieval uses the way 1.5.9 does for a record missing the filtered key.

checklist.claim: Re-importing the same file saves nothing the second time.
checklist.source_excerpt: Re-importing the same file is therefore safe and saves nothing the second time.
checklist.verify_against: import_bundle, dedup_entries and sql_key in src/sqllens/memory/
checklist.verify_hint: Trace a re-import of a file holding a pair whose stored row dedup_entries skips as unreadable, and a pair whose SQL sqlglot regenerates non-deterministically
checklist.evidence: Doc line docs/external/managing-memory.md:126 says 'Re-importing the same file is therefore safe and saves nothing the second time.' The two hinted cases hold: (a) dedup_entries (store.py:199-227) skips only rows with unparseable args_json, non-string/empty sql, or non-string question, but import only writes via add_sql_pair/add_schema_doc from SqlPair/SchemaDoc, whose validators (schema.py:56-57,85-95,119) reject blank text, so import itself does not create skipped rows; (b) sql_key (importer.py:50-64) runs sqlglot.parse + .sql(dialect='mysql') on the same stored text, which is deterministic, and falls back to stripped text, so the key matches on re-import. Counterexample though: the same table (managing-memory.md:121) documents `--clear`, which wipes the collection. import_bundle(clear=True) calls _baseline -> store.clear() then dedup_entries() (importer.py:164-172,202), so existing is empty, _plan puts every item in new_items (importer.py:140-143), and the loop saves all of them (importer.py:211-238, report.saved += 1). So re-importing the same file with --clear saves everything the second time. Also, items whose first-time save failed (importer.py:228-237) are saved on re-import. The absolute wording is therefore false for --clear, though it is accurate for a plain re-import without --clear. Minor doc imprecision; final state is identical.

checklist.claim: export_memories JSON emits sql_pairs via SqlPair.model_dump(exclude_none=True) and schema_docs without training_type, producing a shape parse_json accepts for re-import with groups preserved.
checklist.verify_against: parse_json in src/sqllens/memory/io.py and SqlPair/SchemaDoc fields in schema.py
checklist.verify_hint: Check whether SqlPair has extra fields (e.g. training_type) that model_dump emits and parse_json forbids, and compare with serialize_json
checklist.evidence: admin.py:379-388 export_memories JSON emits {"sql_pairs": [p.model_dump(exclude_none=True)...], "schema_docs": [...exclude training_type]}. SqlPair (schema.py:71-78) has only question/sql/groups, so no training_type leaks there, and SchemaDoc without training_type is accepted (default). BUT parse_json (io.py:153) does MemoryBundle.model_validate(raw), and MemoryBundle.sql_pairs is SqlPairsBlock | None (schema.py:130) with extra=forbid and a `pairs` field (schema.py:96-102). The export emits sql_pairs as a bare list, which fails validation against SqlPairsBlock (an object). So parse_json rejects the exported JSON whenever it is fed back; the claim that it produces a shape parse_json accepts is false. The shape is only the add_memories argument shape (admin.py:18-20), unlike serialize_json (io.py:203-206), which dumps the bundle in the block shape. Requirement: docs/internal/agent/memory.md:176-178 (unchanged in base and head) says JSON is canonical and round-trips losslessly with sql_pairs an object {training_type, pairs}.
